parts.title: Post Office Package Delivery
parts.transcript: Part 1: a customer (Peter White) sends a package to the USA. Service: International Express (3 days), must arrive by Friday. Sender address 14 Mountain Road, Lakeview. Delivery to Anna Hillman, Apartment 228, North Building, Upper Park Avenue, New York. Contents: six books and photographs. Total cost $98. To trace a lost package you give the ID code from the receipt.

parts.transcript: Part 3: Mike discusses his oral history project (local football team, 1983) with his tutor. He used the definition from a lecture handout. The most important internet contribution is the permanent preservation of recordings. He chose the topic because his father loves football. His best information source was the local newspaper archives. He found former players via the phone book (telephone directory). Tutor's feedback on problems: drafted questions too complicated (G); time allotted too long (D); recording equipment too unreliable (A); subjects chosen too vague (H); proposed report too factual, needs his own evaluation (F).

parts.title: Plant Behaviour
parts.transcript: Part 4: lecture on plant behaviour. Scientists once regarded plants as passive organisms; now there is evidence this is untrue. Great Lakes sea rocket grows on beaches; near unrelated plants it grows extra roots to compete for nutrients, but behaves differently with relatives. Sagebrush and thornapple recognise neighbours by the type of light they reflect; possible because each plant has its own signature. The dodder plant cannot produce sugar, so it parasitises other plants; it damages alfalfa, potatoes and citrus; it identifies hosts by detecting the chemicals they give off; it moves in a circle to check the environment then grows toward the best host. Modern equipment now provides evidence of plant behaviour.
